newsitem.title: USA: Sonny Bloch gets 21 month prison term.
newsitem.headline: Sonny Bloch gets 21 month prison term.

text.p: Sonny Bloch, who had been host of one of the nation's longest-running financial talks shows, was sentenced Thursday to 21 months in prison for personal and corporate income tax evasion and lying to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Bloch, 60, who previously pleaded guilty to a total of seven counts, was also sentenced to three years of probation during which time he will provide 750 hours of community service.
"Mr. Bloch is a sophisticated man in the financial arena and he knew exactly how to achieve his tax evasion," said U.S. District Judge Shira Scheindlin in sentencing the radio personality.
Bloch said he had been asked by friends and colleagues why a man who had enjoyed a successful career and was so close to retirement would break the law and risk going to prison.
"The answer is greed and stupidity ... there are no excuses ... just apologies," he said warning colleagues not to "dance with the devil."
He asked for forgiveness from his family, friends and listeners who he described as "these people who gave me the gift of fame and fortune."
Bloch said that the charges end his 38-year career and that all his wealth and success have been "permenantly and justly" taken away by the federal government.
"The Sonny Bloch Show" had been on the air for some 15 years, attracting between 1.3 million and 1.6 million people.
When he pleaded guilty in April, Bloch admitted failing to report $263,406 in personal income tax for the calendar years of 1991, 1992 and 1993.

He also said he had aided Broadcast Mangement Corp., which produced his radio programme, with filing false returns for the same years and evading $146,771. He said he lied to the SEC in 1994 about the income tax returns.
Scheindlin said she was not imposing a fine because of other financial claims against him including $3.9 million by the SEC and $410,000 by the Internal Revenue Service.
Bloch also pleaded guilty last month to a separate case in Newark, N.J. federal court charging him with defrauding listeners of $21 million.
He could be sentenced to more than 30 years for the eight felony charges in that case.

New Jersey prosecutors alleged that Bloch, along with four others coordinated telemarketing efforts to sell fraudulent investments in wireless cable operations and radio stations that Bloch promoted on his radio show from August 1993 to March 1995. Bloch was accused of failing to tell listeners about his involvement in the ventures.

Bloch has also pleaded guilty in a Pennsylvania federal court to conspiracy to commit mail fraud arising from his radio show endorsements. That case carries a possible maximum prison term of five years.

Bloch had left his home in Tampa in 1995 and moved to the Dominican Republic after learning of the federal investigations. He continued to broadcast his show from his new home, but was deported by Dominican Republic authorities in May 1995.
